Certified Kubernetes Application Developer (CKAD) Exam Curriculum

 This document provides the curriculum outline of the Knowledge, Skills and Abilities that
 a Certified Kubernetes Application Developer (CKAD) can be expected to demonstrate.


 CKAD Curriculum

   20% - Application Design and Build                25% - Application Environment,
                                                           Configuration and Security
    • Define, build and modify container images
    • Choose and use the right workload              • Discover and use resources that extend
      resource (Deployment, DaemonSet,                 Kubernetes (CRD, Operators)
      CronJob, etc.)                                 • Understand authentication, authorization
    • Understand multi-container Pod design            and admission control
      patterns (e.g. sidecar, init and others)       • Understand requests, limits, quotas
    • Utilize persistent and ephemeral volumes       • Define resource requirements
                                                     • Understand ConfigMaps
   20% - Application Deployment                      • Create & consume Secrets
                                                     • Understand ServiceAccounts
    • Use Kubernetes primitives to implement         • Understand Application Security
      common deployment strategies (e.g. blue/         (SecurityContexts, Capabilities, etc.)
      green or canary)
    • Understand Deployments and how to
      perform rolling updates                        20% - Services and Networking
    • Use the Helm package manager to deploy
      existing packages                              • Demonstrate basic understanding of
    • Kustomize                                        NetworkPolicies
                                                     • Provide and troubleshoot access to
                                                       applications via services
   15% - Application Observability                   • Use Ingress rules to expose applications
         and Maintenance

    • Understand API depreciations
    • Implement probes and health checks
    • Use built-in CLI tools to monitor Kubernetes
      applications
    • Utilize container logs
    • Debugging in Kubernetes




                                                                                                  2
Cloud native computing uses an open source software stack to
deploy applications as microservices, packaging each part into its
own container, and dynamically orchestrating those containers to
optimize resource utilization. The Cloud Native Computing Foundation
(CNCF) hosts critical components of those software stacks including
Kubernetes, Fluentd, Linkerd, Prometheus, OpenTracing and gRPC;
brings together the industry’s top developers, end users, and vendors;
and serves as a neutral home for collaboration. CNCF is part of The
Linux Foundation, a nonprofit organization. For more information
about CNCF, please visit: https://cncf.io/.
